facts.evidence: **Diluted Earnings per Share**: $4.81, up 32% on a GAAP basis, and $4.74, up 23% on a non-GAAP basis

**Microsoft Cloud and AI**: Revenue of $59.3 billion, up 27% year-over-year, with Azure and other cloud services revenue increasing 43%
**Microsoft Cloud and AI**: Revenue of $59.3 billion, up 27% year-over-year
**More Personal Computing**: Revenue of $12.9 billion, down 4% (5% in constant currency)

claims.claim: Fourth quarter revenue was $90.0 billion.
Fourth quarter revenue increased 18% year over year.
Fourth quarter revenue increased 17% in constant currency.
Fourth quarter operating income was $40.6 billion.
Fourth quarter operating income increased 18% year over year.
Fourth quarter net income was $35.8 billion and increased 31% on a GAAP basis.
Fourth quarter net income was $35.3 billion and increased 22% on a non-GAAP basis.
Fourth quarter diluted earnings per share was $4.81 and increased 32% on a GAAP basis.
Fourth quarter diluted earnings per share was $4.74 and increased 23% on a non-GAAP basis.
Microsoft Cloud revenue was $59.3 billion, up 27% year over year.
claims.note: Figures match; note the brief lists 'Microsoft Cloud and AI' among segments, whereas the release reports Microsoft Cloud as a cross-segment metric and its three segments are Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud and More Personal Computing.

claims.claim: Azure and other cloud services revenue increased 43% year over year.
Productivity and Business Processes revenue was $37.8 billion, up 14%.
Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue grew 16%, and 14% on a reported basis.
Productivity and Business Processes growth was driven by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue growth.
claims.note: The release presents Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud as a business highlight of the segment; the brief's 'driven by' framing is a fair paraphrase of that presentation.

claims.claim: More Personal Computing revenue was $12.9 billion, down 4% year over year.
More Personal Computing revenue was down 5% in constant currency.
Windows OEM and Devices revenue decreased 7%.
No guidance or outlook was provided in the release.
claims.note: Correct that the release contains no forward guidance figures, though the release states guidance will be provided on the earnings call and webcast, which the brief omits.

claims.claim: Fiscal year revenue was $331.8 billion, up 18%.
Fiscal year revenue was up 16% in constant currency.
Fiscal year operating income was $155.2 billion, up 21%.
Fiscal year operating income was up 19% in constant currency.
Fiscal year net income was $133.7 billion, up 31% on a GAAP basis.
Fiscal year net income was up 22% (20% in constant currency) on a non-GAAP basis.
Fiscal year diluted earnings per share was $17.95, up 32% on a GAAP basis.
Fiscal year diluted earnings per share was up 22% (21% in constant currency) on a non-GAAP basis.
The release does not provide any guidance for future quarters.
claims.note: No guidance figures appear in the release; the release does say guidance will be given on the conference call.

claims.claim: Azure and other cloud services showed continued strong growth.
claims.note: Supported by the 43% quarterly growth and the statement that Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time this year; the release shows no prior-quarter growth rates, so 'continued' rests on those two datapoints.

claims.claim: Revenue in More Personal Computing is declining.
